verifications.claim: Artemis II is a ~10-day crewed mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "over the course of about a 10-day mission" (R1); "historic 10-day mission" (R2); "Duration: 10 days" (R3); "lasting about 10 days" (R4); "nine-day trip" but contextually ~10 days (R5); "expected to last about 10 days" (R6); "10-day trip" (R7); "10-day mission" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state approximately 10-day duration for the crewed mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled for April 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "By April 2026" (R3); "as early as April 1" (R4); "launched... April" context 2026 (R5); "launching... April-1" (R6); "launches Wednesday... April" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently reference April 2026 launch window.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will send four astronauts around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "four astronauts will confirm... deep space" around Moon (R1); "four astronauts... circle it" (R2); "carrying four astronauts on a journey around the Moon" (R3); "send four astronauts around the moon" (R4); "crew of four astronauts on a trailblazing nine-day trip around the moon" (R5); "four astronauts" flyby (R6); "four astronauts... around the Moon" (R7); "crew of four astronauts... around the Moon" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm four astronauts on lunar flyby mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first human journey beyond low-Earth orbit since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first flight to the moon since 1972" (R4); "first crew to head for the moon since... 1972" (R5); "first crewed journey beyond low Earth orbit since... 1972" (R6); "first humans back to the Moon in over 50 years" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported as first beyond LEO since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will launch on the SLS rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Orion spacecraft, Space Launch System (SLS) rocket" (R1); "NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket will launch... Orion" (R3); "NASA's new Space Launch System rocket... Orion capsule" (R4); "NASA's Space Launch System rocket... Orion" (R5); "Space Launch System rocket... Orion spacecraft" (R6); "NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket... Orion" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Universally stated across sources.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will perform Earth-orbit system checks.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "verify that all systems are performing as expected" (R3); "system checks to confirm... life-support systems, propulsion, and communications" (R6); "checkouts on Orion’s systems" (R5); "circling Earth... system checks" implied (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Initial Earth orbits dedicated to system checks explicitly described.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will execute a translunar injection.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "final push to enter lunar orbit" TLI (R3); "Orion's main engine will hurl the crew to the moon... trans-lunar injection" (R4); "trans-lunar injection, or TLI, burn" (R5,R6); "translunar injection burn" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: TLI burn explicitly named and described.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will perform a crewed lunar flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "around the Moon" (R1); "fly around our natural satellite" (R3); "lunar fly-around" "lunar flyby" (R4); "flying around the moon" (R5); "lunar flyby" (R6); "fly by the lunar far side" (R8); "around the farside of the Moon" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Core mission profile is crewed lunar flyby.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will return to a Pacific Ocean splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown... Pacific" (R4); "Pacific Ocean splashdown" (R5); "parachuting into the Pacific Ocean" (R6); "splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently Pacific Ocean splashdown.

verifications.claim: On Day 1 of Artemis II, the SLS rocket places Orion into an initial high-Earth orbit.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "first 25 hours circling Earth in a high, lopsided orbit" (R4); "set the spacecraft on an elliptical orbit with a high point of 43,760 miles" Day 1 (R5); "SLS rocket will place Orion into an initial orbit around Earth. During the first day or two" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: SLS places into initial orbit on Day 1, subsequent burns create high-Earth orbit within first ~24 hours, but not explicitly 'high-Earth' solely by SLS.

verifications.claim: During Days 1-2 of Artemis II, astronauts will separate from the ICPS upper stage, as reported by NASA and PBS News.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "separated upper stage" first 25 hours (R4 PBS); "separated from the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage... about three hours and 23 minutes after launch" (R5 NASA)
verifications.reasoning: Separation occurs early Day 1 (within Days 1-2), cited sources confirm.

verifications.claim: During Days 1-2 of Artemis II, astronauts will manually fly the spacecraft around the ICPS to test maneuvering capabilities, as reported by NASA and PBS News.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "take manual control... proximity operations demonstration" (R3); "manually fly... around the ICPS" (R4 PBS); "test the Orion's maneuvering system, approaching and flying around the spent SLS upper stage" (R5 NASA)
verifications.reasoning: Manual fly-around of ICPS explicitly in initial phase (Days 1-2), cited sources.

verifications.claim: On Day 2 of Artemis II, Orion fires its engines to leave Earth's orbit and enter a free-return trajectory toward the Moon, according to WESH 2 News.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "trans-lunar injection burn... about 24 hours after launch" "free-return lunar flyby" (R6 WESH)
verifications.reasoning: Exactly matches Day 2 TLI for free-return, cited source.

verifications.claim: On Day 6 of Artemis II, the crew will swing around the far side of the Moon, notes the Planetary Society.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "around the farside of the Moon... April 6" (assuming launch April 1, Day 6) (R9 Planetary)
verifications.reasoning: Lunar flyby around far side on Day 6, cited source.

verifications.claim: During the Artemis II lunar flyby on Day 6, the crew reaches distances up to 450,000 km from Earth, notes the Planetary Society.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "maximum distance from Earth at 406,771 kilometers" (R9 Planetary); "5,000 miles (8,000 kilometers) beyond the moon" ~392k km (R4); "252,000 miles" ~406k km (R5)
verifications.reasoning: R9 specifies 406,771 km max, not 450,000 km; other sources align ~400k km.

verifications.claim: On Day 10 of Artemis II, the spacecraft returns to Earth, hitting the atmosphere at roughly 25,000 mph (7 miles/second), as described by CBS News.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "moving at some 25,000 mph — roughly 7 miles per second — when it slams back into... atmosphere... end of the mission on Friday, April 10" Day 10 (R5 CBS)
verifications.reasoning: Exact speed and Day 10 reentry, cited source.

verifications.claim: On Day 10 of Artemis II, the spacecraft endures temperatures near 5,000°F during re-entry, as described by CBS News.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "heat shield endures temperatures as high as 5,000 degrees" reentry Day 10 (R5 CBS)
verifications.reasoning: Exact temperature and timing, cited source.

verifications.claim: Artemis II involves validating life-support, navigation, and propulsion systems with a human crew for the first time in deep space, according to ESA.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "test the capabilities of the Orion spacecraft and its European Service Module, now fitted with life support systems"; "verify that all systems are performing as expected" first crewed (R3 ESA)
verifications.reasoning: ESA source confirms life support and propulsion testing first crewed deep space, navigation implied in checks/manual control, but not explicitly listed.

verifications.claim: Artemis II involves testing manual controls for the spacecraft, per NASA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "take manual control of the spacecraft to conduct a proximity operations demonstration" (R3); "manually fly the spacecraft" (R4); manual maneuvering (R5 NASA sources)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit manual control testing described.

verifications.claim: A core objective of Artemis II is gathering data to prepare for Artemis III by ensuring safe landing of the first woman and next man on the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "pave the way to land the first woman and next man on the Moon on Artemis III" (R1); "data will directly inform... Artemis III... land astronauts on the Moon" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Directly states paving way for first woman/next man landing on Artemis III.
